title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X/S is a relative elliptic curve over a base of characteristic 0. S' ⊂ X is the finite étale degree-3 subscheme of nonzero 2-torsion points. J is the generalized Jacobian (Rosenlicht–Serre) of X with modulus the reduced divisor S'. J° is its degree-0 part.

Step 1, structure of J°. J° is an extension of X by a torus (302):
1 → J°_0 → J° → X → 1, with J°_0 ≅ G_m ⊗_Z M_0.
Here M_0 = M_0(X/S) is the rank-2 étale-local lattice defined in (299). For a degree-3 modulus the torus is R_{S'/S}G_m / G_m, so M_0 should be the cocharacter lattice Z^{S'}/Z (equivalently the dual of the degree-zero divisors on S').

The point of the construction: the three 2-torsion points (equivalently the roots e1, e2, e3 of the Weierstrass cubic) define a relative P^1 with three marked points. That is the same kind of datum as the type-(0,3) curves X̃/S of the previous page, for which M_0, M_1 and the 'Fermat tower' torsors F_∞(X̃/S) (301) were defined. So M_0 is the same lattice in both settings.

Step 2, Tate modules. Take n-torsion. Multiplication by n is surjective on the torus, so the snake lemma gives exact sequences 0 → T[n] → J°[n] → X[n] → 0. Passing to the limit over finite groups gives (303):
1 → M_1 → T_∞(J°) → T_∞(X) → 1, with M_1 = M_0 ⊗ T_∞(G_m) = M_0 ⊗ Ẑ(1).
Here T_∞(G) = lim_n {}_nG (304). In characteristic 0 this is the local system of fibrewise fundamental groups of a smooth commutative group scheme with connected fibres.

Step 3, torsors. By general nonsense for an extension 1→A→B→C→1 of commutative groups, A-torsors are equivalent to B-torsors P together with a section of the induced C-torsor P/A, via P ↦ P ×^A B. So an M_1-torsor (such as a Fermat torsor F_∞) is the same as a T_∞(J°)-torsor plus a trivialization of its pushforward to T_∞(X).

Step 4, the open question. Is there a reasonable description of the Fermat torsors F_∞(X/S) in terms of the geometry of the elliptic curve X/S? The natural candidates are Kummer-type torsors of division points of suitable points of J°, which would be a kind of elliptic / generalized-Jacobian incarnation of the abelianized Galois action on π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}).

Next page (§14) carries this out for the generalized Jacobian of U_{0,3} itself: J* with J^0 ≅ G_m ⊗ M, the Abel–Jacobi map φ: U_{0,3} → J^1 and the S_3-action. A marginal note on the previous page points to a 'geometric variant' at (320), p. 724.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. The exactness of (303) needs only n-divisibility of the torus, which holds. The torsor equivalence is correct because the groups are commutative.

Minor imprecision: whether M_0 is the character or cocharacter lattice of the torus J°_0 depends on the convention in (299), which is not visible here. Writing G_m ⊗ M_0 makes it the cocharacter lattice.
The identification of T_∞(G) with π_1 of the fibres is valid in characteristic 0, as assumed. In positive characteristic one would need the prime-to-p part.

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks for a description of the Fermat-tower torsor F_∞ (a torsor under M_0⊗Ẑ(1) attached to a three-pointed relative P^1) in terms of the generalized Jacobian of an elliptic curve with modulus at its 2-torsion. He reduces it to a T(J°)-torsor plus a trivialization over T(X). This is an explicit program linking the abelianized Galois action on π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) (Fermat curves, Jacobi sums) to 1-motives over the moduli of elliptic curves (Legendre/level-2 structure), with S_3-equivariance.
missed.quote: Y a-t-il une description raisonnable des torseurs de Fermat F_∞(X/S), en termes de la géométrie de la courbe elliptique relative X/S ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Anderson's hyperadelic gamma function and Ihara's work describe the Fermat tower through generalized Jacobians of P^1 minus 3 points. A uniform description over M_{1,1} via the extension J° of X by a rank-2 torus would put the Fermat/Jacobi-sum Galois data in a family of 1-motives over the modular curve. This could connect to elliptic polylogarithms and elliptic Kummer classes (Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto). I am not aware of this exact formulation being worked out, though partial analogues exist.

deep.surprise_reason: The constructions on the page are standard (generalized Jacobian, Tate modules of a 1-motive, torsor reduction). The interest is the posed question of realizing the Fermat-tower torsor through the generalized Jacobian of an elliptic curve with modulus at 2-torsion. It anticipates themes later developed independently (Anderson, Ihara, elliptic analogues), but it is only a question here.
transcription_corrections: 'en termes de la C géométrie' should read 'en termes de la géométrie' (the 'C' is a stray letter).
The inserted phrase reads 'des schémas en groupes lisses comm. à fibres connexes sur S'; the insertion '{+à fibres connexes+}' belongs before 'sur S'.
In (302) the kernel is J°_0 (torus part), noted ≅ G_m ⊗_Z M_0 below it; in (303) M_1 is noted '= M_0 ⊗_Z T_∞(G_m)' below it.
Equation number (304) was overwritten/corrected in the manuscript.
